- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in subsequent periods.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤-1.0) or mixed, model often underestimates downside risk; add 3–7% buffer to forecast lows.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3–5 days); apply “lag correction” by subtracting 2–5% from forecast 3–7 days post-spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30-day forecast is >10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 3–6% unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- For 30-day horizon, model underperforms when sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-horizon; adjust downward by 2–5% in 15–25 day window.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “bullish → bearish” transitions, model tends to overreact; dampen forecast slope in 10–15 day window.
